newsitem.title: KENYA: Exporter sales lift Kenya shilling against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Exporter sales lift Kenya shilling against dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling strengthened slightly against the dollar and the pound on Friday in a moderately active market, dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 55.94 against the dollar from 55.97 on Thursday, and of 87.57 to the pound from 87.66 on Thursday.
A commercial banker said interbank activity was moderate with inflows of hard currency pushing the dollar down.
"The shilling continued its bullish drive against the dollar and other hard currencies with renewed exporter sales into the market," a dealer said.
"The market opened at 55.95/10 and closed a relatively busy day at 55.85/00," he said.
Another dealer added: "In the absence of further intervention we are likely to see the dollar depreciate further next week.
Dealers said overnight money market rates remained at 10-15 percent levels.
